dispatch.comment: Numbers of the hand-written theorem `enter` (Enter.lean): gas of the prelude, gas of one table entry, the memory words after the prelude (free memory pointer 0x60), the least call data size of `enter` (the code has no test for 4 bytes), and the line of ok_<fn> that proves it.
dispatch.size_proof: have hsize : 1 ≤ message.data.size := size_of_selector hsel (by decide)

paths.comment: memory_lemmas named: the block lemmas use the lemmas named after the offset of the free memory pointer (memW_ext96, memW_write96, memW_read96, size_memW4) where they apply, as the first build of this token did; without the key the lemmas for any aligned word are used (memW_set, memW_readWord, size_memWn).

functions.name: withdrawEther
functions.frame_comment: frame: true = the path of this function stops at its CALL (gen_paths.py has no rule for a message). What it weakens: no generated ok_withdrawEther (completeness for successful runs), no generated supply_withdrawEther, no generated witness; supply_preserved takes the hypothesis selector != 0x3bed33ce. What stands for them, hand-written and in the axioms test: frame_theorems (Bnb/Withdraw.lean), the sequence theorems of Bnb/Seq.lean and the witnesses of Bnb/Sanity/Withdraw.lean.

axioms.comment: names: hand-written theorems checked before the generated ones; after: theorems of files that import the generated ones; imports: modules Test/Axioms.lean imports first (gen_axioms.py adds every module of the root file, and a scan of every constant of them). There is no skip list: withdrawEther (frame: true) has no generated ok_ and supply_ theorem, and names the hand-written ones under frame_theorems.

sanity.comment: The witness call of each function (scripts/gen_sanity.py). A list: the argument words, on the state with every slot 0. A dict: args, and state = the slots that hold the word 5 (MASK is the 160 bit mask); every amount is 1.
sanity.doc:
`<fn>_runs`: in a state with one account at the contract `C`, where the slots listed in
`config/bnb.json` (`sanity.<fn>.state`) hold the word 5 and every other slot 0, the call of `<fn>`
with the argument words below (every amount is 1, so tokens really move) meets every hypothesis
of the success path theorem of `<fn>`; so there is a run from pc 0 that ends with no error and
with the stated output. No fact about keccak is used: a slot is the term `mapSlot ...`, whatever
its number is, and the proofs hold whether or not two of these slots are the same slot.

state: mapSlot (bitwiseAnd MASK (bitwiseAnd MASK (bitwiseAnd MASK (2 : U256)))) (5 : U256)
mapSlot (bitwiseAnd MASK (bitwiseAnd MASK caller.toU256)) (mapSlot (bitwiseAnd MASK (bitwiseAnd MASK (bitwiseAnd MASK (2 : U256)))) (7 : U256))
